Domain, Path, Secure, SameSite

Five cookies from shop.example.com

  1. 1__Host-sid: Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, Lax
  2. 2cart: Domain=example.com, Secure, Strict
  3. 3prefs: Path=/account, Lax
  4. 4widget: Domain=example.com, Secure, None
  5. 5theme: no Secure, Lax

Internet & networking · 3/8

Domain and Path pick the URL

Domain

  • No Domain: host-only
  • Domain=example.com: subdomains too
  • Never a public suffix like com

Path

  • Path=/account matches /account/orders
  • It does not match /
  • It does not match /accounts

Path is not a security boundary

Internet & networking · 4/8

Secure and HttpOnly do different jobs

Secure

  • Sent only on https requests
  • Except on localhost
  • http pages cannot set it

HttpOnly

  • Page scripts cannot read it
  • Script requests still send it
  • Limits damage from XSS

HttpOnly controls JavaScript, not the request

Internet & networking · 5/8

SameSite looks at where the request starts

  1. 1Same site: shop.example.com and blog.example.com
  2. 2Strict: same-site requests only
  3. 3Lax: plus cross-site top-level navigation with GET
  4. 4None: every request, Secure required

Internet & networking · 8/8

Name prefixes force safe attributes

__Secure-

  • Needs Secure
  • Set from an https page
  • Domain is allowed

__Host-

  • Needs Secure
  • Needs Path=/
  • No Domain: host-only

__Host- treats the origin as the boundary

The browser stores cookies.

Before each request, it checks every stored cookie

and sends only the cookies that pass.

Here are five cookies from shop.example.com.

Each line shows the attributes that the Set-Cookie header gave the cookie.

Without Domain, a cookie goes only to the host that set it.

With Domain, subdomains get it too.

Path=/account matches /account and its subpaths.

Secure sends the cookie only over https.

HttpOnly hides the cookie from page scripts,

but their requests still carry it.

A site is the scheme plus the registrable domain.

Strict stays same-site.

Lax also allows cross-site top-level GET navigations.

None allows every request and needs Secure.

A link on news.other.org opens shop.example.com.

The Strict cart cookie stays home.

Lax and None cookies go with the GET navigation.

Now a form on other.org sends a POST.

POST is not a safe method, so Lax cookies stay home.

Only the None cookie goes.

The browser rejects a __Secure- cookie without Secure.

A __Host- cookie also needs Path=/ and no Domain,

so only its own host gets it.
